A commenter praised PostHog's self-built community forum UI: big tech Q&A or knowledge-base forums usually have terrible design, while PostHog's is "appropriately dense and easy to navigate. Nice job."

Complaint about PostHog's new forum: it doesn't render without JavaScript, so it isn't archived on archive.org and probably isn't searchable via Bing or DuckDuckGo. This undercuts the stated goal of making solutions searchable.

A commenter questioned PostHog building its own forum on Strapi instead of using Discourse or another off-the-shelf tool. They argued it means rebuilding login, user management, moderation and threads from scratch, with the bugs that come with that, taking time away from the core products.
"I've been using PostHog with my app for about a week now, and so far the results have been good. Pretty straightforward to integrate with a Swift iOS app too!"
"Looks pretty sweet. I like the UI for adding event captures."
A user tried the docker deploy command from the landing page and found it "super easy to get up and running." They wished for a sample dataset to explore the UI before deploying to Heroku.
Bug report: the production Dockerfile and posthog/posthog:latest image were "busted" and didn't create any database. The user spent an hour debugging and asked that the README mention it.
A user reported that PostHog's sign-up page appeared broken in Firefox and shared a screenshot.
"Great idea to be compatible with Mixpanel libraries! Makes switching over really easy"

A former Heap engineer warned that query performance would be a major scaling challenge for PostHog: without multi-tenancy, a query can't use a large shared cluster. In their view, Postgres-based PostHog would work fine for modest data volumes (around <5GB) but struggle at multi-terabyte scale.

A user tried PostHog's LLM integration to create a user cohort from a SQL query. It said it couldn't create cohorts, and a cohort can't use a SQL query, so they had to export data from a SQL insight instead. Worse, typing in the text input dropped their M4 Pro to under 1 fps after two prompts, which "left a bad taste."
Commenters criticized PostHog's website: one said the blog post page broke scrolling, and another said "I cannot believe they're sticking to their guns on this website design. It's awful."
